pr_title: server: support deprecation of EOF packets
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Adds support for `CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF`

Issue Number: close #32118

Note that  #32119 has a different solution to the same problem

Related: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_basic_response_packets.html

Problem Summary:

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note
Support for the CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF feature of the MySQL protocol was added.
```

issue_context.title: server: support `CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF` capability flag
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

MySQL deprecated `EOF` packets since MySQL v5.7.5 and [`CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF`](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/internals/en/capability-flags.html) was introduced since then.

This flag, as well as the deprecation of EOF was not supported by TiDB. This is fine since this flag requires a server-client negotiation according to the MySQL protocol. All MySQL clients are able to communicate with TiDB by treating it as 'the old MySQL server'.

However, it is better to make it implemented for:
* EOF has been deprecated for a long time, we hope that TiDB could be 'up-to-date' for MySQL compatibilities.
* The 'old server' might not be fully tested for the new versions of MySQL clients. For example: [Connector/J bug #10625](https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=106252)
comments: @bb7133 I'm also interested in working on this

review_comments:
You mean `writeOkWithHeader` or `writeWithHeader`?

I think the current name is fine as it is always an `OK_Packet`, but with two kinds of headers (0x00, OK or 0xFE EOF). This is done in a weird way in the protocol, but that's just how it is.

See also:
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_basic_ok_packet.html
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_basic_eof_packet.html

I'd like to keep the current name if that's ok with you
That is not strictly needed, but when `ClientDeprecateEOF` is active this code shouldn't be reached, if it is there is likely a bug, so I added this to make that visible. We could remove this.
@bb7133 what do you think? keep this? remove this? Could you suggest other reviewers as well?

Hi, according to the MySQL doc https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_com_stmt_prepare.html#sect_protocol_com_stmt_prepare_response.

> if num_params > 0 and CLIENT_OPTIONAL_RESULTSET_METADATA is not set or if medatdata_follows is RESULTSET_METADATA_FULL num_params packets will follow. Then a [EOF_Packet](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_basic_eof_packet.html) will be transmitted, provided that CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF is not set.

It seems we always send num_params packets? So, we always send EOF when ClientDeprecateEOF  is disable. why can this work?

There is no `CLIENT_OPTIONAL_RESULTSET_METADATA` defined in TiDB yet.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/37bd052ee53d1180a89e12b6a01a2ec854f357b6/parser/mysq/const.go#L163

I think the second sentence in that quote is not dependent on the first part.

So maybe read it like:

> if num_params > 0 and CLIENT_OPTIONAL_RESULTSET_METADATA is not set or if medatdata_follows is RESULTSET_METADATA_FULL num_params packets will follow.

> Then a [EOF_Packet](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_basic_eof_packet.html) will be transmitted, provided that CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF is not set.


And when we exclude `CLIENT_OPTIONAL_RESULTSET_METADATA` and `medatdata_follows` (which requires the former) then it is like this:

> if num_params > 0, num_params packets will follow.

> Then a [EOF_Packet](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_basic_eof_packet.html) will be transmitted, provided that CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF is not set.

This seems to match what the code does.

Would be good to compare this with MySQL packet traces if you think MySQL is behaving differently.
